The way a decentralized reddit works is like this. Each user has an app, the reddit app, which connects to the reddit p2p network. For most users, the app is a normal web app. Each user funds their own app with a small amount of bitcoin. In order to download content, the user pays a very, very small amount of bitcoin to the peers on the network. This incentivizes people to keep the app open so as to keep servicing the other users. Furthermore, when a user upvotes content, that sends a small amount of bitcoin to the author of that content, thus incentivizing the production of good content. If all the content is authenticated, we can be reasonably sure most payments are going to the right people.

This is the near term endgame for reddit-type content aggregators. The first aggregator that fits the above description to achieve critical mass will be the undisputed successor to the reddit empire. @Atko et al., take note!

It's not just Reddit but the entire internet since crypto could become a missing payment layer of the web proposed in projects like Xanadu while simultaneously incentivizing decentralization alongside meshnets.

Its fucking WH40K, but in FANTASY. Basically GW went "We want the WH40K audience"

I think it's a great idea. I've been a 40k player for years, but always interested in Fantasy. I didn't want to commit to another super-involved game though. Now that the rules are free, and seemingly accessible to the Fantasy newbie, I think I might buy some models and give it a go.

Everything I've heard and all the people I've talked to that have played it conclude that it cannot be competitive in any realistic way. However, they did an absolutely AMAZING job designing the models that come with the AOS box set. So here's to beautiful things.

I'm speaking as a competitive-only tournament player, located in the North-East USA.

This game's rules are a joke. It has zero strategic depth, zero "theoryhammer", and no way at all to balance competitive armies against each other. This game is a blatant "FUCK YOU" to every hardcore WHFB player in the world. The silly rules in the warscrolls, the new direction for the art and sculpting, the re-spelling of all the factions (Ogors, Aelfs), all of this is intended to make your old army worthless and useless. In 12-18 months you're going to see it for what it really is: total system reboot, all your previous money spent on models and books completely wasted.

I'm playing Kings of War now. If you still want to play a game where precise movement and facing matters, where you're rewarded for making a plan and executing it, where carefully crafting a list for the metagame matters, and all the things that made WHFB 8th edition a fun competitive game, go play Kings of War.

If you just wanna smash dollies together and laugh, play Age of Sigmar. Personally, if I just want to smash dollies together, Ill go play GI Joes with my 5 year old son.

I'm with you. I'm not, nor have I ever been a competitive-only player, but I agree that Age of Sigmar is disgusting. A competitive rules set has never hurt a game.

I could have handled a skirmish/smaller model count version of Warhammer, but this Chutes+Ladders approach to gaming is disappointing. You're right, if I wanted to play make believe or whatever, I can do it without 40 dollar dice shakers.

The writing's on the wall, and I'd be a fool to think that Age of Sigmar isn't a taste of what's to come for 40k as well. I'm done with Games Workshop. I'll keep playing 40k, but I won't be buying anything from them in the future.

I'm also very interested in the new Kings of War rules and trying out a game.
